g.text: One sentence. e.g. For the results check, what precision and recall must we reach?
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
Why decide now? Facts and constraints: earlier ADRs, data, law, budget, people. What goes wrong if we don't decide? 3–6 lines.
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
Mark it "(current proposal)" if it is.
Mark it "(current proposal)" if it is.
Mark it "(current proposal)" if it is.
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
Quality: does it meet our targets?
Cost: money, tokens, time per run
Risk: what breaks, who gets hurt
Effort: to build and to maintain
Undo: how hard to reverse later
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose option _ because … One paragraph. Name the criteria from the grid that decided it.
Easier: what gets simpler or becomes possible.
Harder: what gets more difficult, costs more, or is ruled out.
Revisit when: evidence that would change this decision, e.g. a metric crossing a value, a new
Lab: the code or eval run that tested this decision (file or commit) and its result in one line. No lab,
Questions raised, ideas rejected and why, points for later ADRs.

How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision
is too big, so split it.
